typecheck.why: A type error is the cheapest failure to catch and the one a stage meets most while it works.

lint.why: Typed rules read the whole program, so a change in one file can raise a finding in another: the full check lints every file, and turn end only lints what changed.

unused.why: knip counts its entries from the registered parts, so code only a test reaches is refused while the session that wrote it can still wire it or delete it.

written-twice.why: A string one owner writes and another reads, spelled twice, drifts; it is cheap enough to hold every turn.

test.why: The whole suite, which drives real processes and takes minutes, so it runs in the full check only; fast false keeps the related tests the fast check would find out of the turn end, where one changed file reaches 19 test files and a minute.

prompts.why: Every stage prompt stays under its byte cap with its slots filled to their caps.

links.why: Every part links a failure that exists on GitHub, which needs the network and gh, so it runs in the full check only.

rulesets.why: main's ruleset lives on GitHub, not in this tree, so no change here turns it red or green; it reads the network through gh, which the test step's receipts cannot trace, so it runs in the full check only and a doc-only change runs no test file.
